newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes Aviation to expand service.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes Aviation to expand service.

text.p: Great Lakes Aviation, operating as United Express, said it would expand its service to two more cities over this weekend, following a voluntary suspension of service that began May 16.
Great Lakes voluntarily suspended service when the Federal Aviation Administration told the carrier it faced a suspension of its operating authority due to flying unworthy aircraft.
It said it resumed service to Lansing, Mich. and Decatur, Ill. on Saturday and would resume service to Traverse City, Mich. on Tuesday, May 27.
On Friday, it said it would resume limited service to five cities in Iowa and Illinois.
It would fly Beechcraft 1900Ds, which carry 19 passengers and had an average age of under two years.

Great Lakes, which operates as United Express in the midwest, as Midway Connection in the southeast and as Great Lakes Airlines regionally, expects to gradually increase service as the company completes its inspections of the airline's fleet, which are monitored by the FAA.
